steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Butter a 2-quart casserole dish.
Combine sweet potatoes, eggs, white sugar, heavy cream, and vanilla extract in a bowl; transfer to the prepared dish.
Combine pecans, brown sugar, flour, and butter; mix until crumbly. Sprinkle over sweet potato mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Praline Sweet Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: In this recipe for sweet potatoes with a candied pecan crust, the potatoes are whipped with cream, butter and eggs, and baked in a casserole with a pecan and brown sugar topping.
raw_recipe.name: Praline Sweet Potatoes

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Butter a 2-quart casserole dish.
Combine sweet potatoes, eggs, white sugar, heavy cream, and vanilla extract in a bowl; transfer to the prepared dish.
Combine pecans, brown sugar, flour, and butter; mix until crumbly. Sprinkle over sweet potato mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes.

review.reviewBody: Wow! This was the hit of Thanksgiving! It is very creamy and rich, so if you don't care for very sweet sweet potatoes, I suggest omitting the 1/2 c. of white sugar. I only used 1T of vanilla (that was plenty!), 3 extra large eggs, and added a sprinkle of cinnamon. I do think that the recipe is a bit vague when it came to the topping though. My topping came out perfectly and here's what I did. I let the butter come to room temp and cubed it. I mixed it with the other topping ingredients until the butter was well blended, there should be no loose flour or sugar. I baked it uncovered and had to let it go about 45 minutes. At 30 minutes, the top was still watery. You MUST leave it in until the topping is crisp on the edges and firm in the middle, that’s what makes it so good. I didn't see a need to double the topping recipe. This recipe is perfect to make the day before. Just make the sweet potato part, cover, and put in the refrigerator overnight. Make the topping right before you pop it in the oven and it’s perfect!

AWESOME! I did make a few changes. I used brown sugar instead of white and used only two eggs to give it more of a mashed sweet potato feel instead of a pie texture. Oh, I cut the vanilla back to one tablespoon, it's plenty.I also added 1/4 teaspoon salt, it really enhances the flavor. I've made this many times and I never used all the topping,
I like it to resemble a side dish, not dessert. But everyone loves it and we have it numerous times throughout the winter months. Thank you!

I made this recipe and it was heavenly!!! But being in french culinary school I knew I might be able to make this a little more flavorful! So I used fresh baked sweet potatoes, and since they can be stringy I put about 3/4 of this mixture into the blender, this made the texture incredible creamy! Also another amazing thing to do is cream together the sugar and egg yolks, until ribbons form that melt back into the mixture, this is how . Also To make this especially fluffy, add the egg whites to a electric mixer and mix just until stiff peaks form ( fold this into the sweet potato mixture very last and don't over mix it!) This dish NEEDS salt (to taste) to bring out the natural sweet flavor of the potatoes. Also for acid I added the juice from a quarter of a lemon, and a couple table spoons of Gran Mariner.!!!

This recipe has been a staple in our house for 20 years! sometimes I make it using canned sweet potatoes, I use 2-29oz cans and I drain them. This is a hair quicker and the difference from using fresh cooked is MINIMAL!! The time savings is worth it! Also, I usually make this dish on Monday! I save the praline part in a zip-loc and I put it all in the fridge. I pull them out Thanksgiving morning and when the praline mix warms up a bit, I cover the casserole and leave it on the counter to come to room temp before I put it in the oven to bake. This recipe is a HUGE hit and one I make every year!

I researched the many various recipes and reviews for this sweet potato dish, and read all the reviews here before making this last night. All the previous times I tried to make it, it never came out. It did this time! I used 2- 29oz cans of yams (drained & dried) that made exactly 4 cups mashed. Big time saver to use canned. Recipe states to use 2 quart casserole but I think it would go better in a 9x13 but you'd have to double the topping. The only changes I made was I used 3 eggs, 1 1/2 teaspoons very good vanilla, 1/2 cup white sugar AND 1/2 cup light brown sugar for the base, also evaporated milk. I wanted mine to be more like dessert. Most recipes call for 1 cup of white sugar & only 3 cups mashed potato's. I did bake it for 60 minutes but 45 would have been better. This is very delicious- hot or cold. I will try to make it again with Splenda.

I have made this multiple holidays and have been asked to bring it again. Best tip is to use a food processor for the filling. Throw it all in there and blend until smooth. I have used fresh sweet potatoes as well as bagged frozen streamable cubes. When I bake the fresh sweet potatoes, I leave them until there is stuff bursting from the skin. I basically forget they're in the oven until I remember again. This brings their natural sugars out. I have even left out a 1/4-1/2 cup of sugar doing this and no one noticed.

I make this every year for Christmas and we love it! However, I do think it needs a couple of tweaks. The main one is it needs salt for contrast. I recommend reading the review by the French pastry chef. It also needs to be cooked a lot longer than the recipe says. I cook it an hour or more, until the topping becomes crispy or crunchy. This recipe is very forgiving and fun to alter - add eggnog instead of cream (cut back on sugar), add pineapple, add cinnamon, etc.... You can also easily make this gluten free (which is what I do). I just use any gluten free flour in place of the regular flour and it works like a charm. All the gluten lovers in the family can't even tell.

Everyone loved this recipe! Very very good. Easy to make up ahead and sprinkle the topping on just before you pop it in the oven. 

I cut the white sugar in half and you could even use less and it would still be very good. Used a scant cup of brown sugar for the topping and had some of that left. Everyone had seconds! YUM!!

This was the 2nd year I made this recipe. This year I followed another reviewer and put all of my ingredients in my mixer and mixed everything until smooth. I baked 4 pounds of sweet potatoes which equaled 4 cups. I also added cinnamon, nutmeg and a little more brown sugar (couple of teaspoons-to taste). Last year, I was told that it was okay-it could have been sweeter but that was my fault because I totally screwed the topping up. However, this year I made it again and EVERYONE loved it. The topping was delicious, the potatoes were so smooth and creamy. I will probably cut back on the butter (maybe 3/4 stick of butter-rather than an entire stick) for the topping but besides that it was soooooo yummy. Thank you for sharing this yummy recipe!

I made this dish for our Thanksgiving dinner and we ready enjoyed it! I followed the suggestion to cut the sugar and decrease the amount of vanilla from the sweet potato portion, which was perfect and allowed us to enjoy the naturally sweet flavor of the potatoes. Also made that portion ahead the day before, so it was quite easy to finish up on the busy day of our dinner celebration. The praline top was just the right amount of sweet!

My entire family LOVED this recipe! It was such a hit. I used my mix master fitted with the wire whisk attachment to cream all the casserole ingredients together, and it worked really well. It turned out so smooth and creamy. I added about 3 tsp of cinnamon, and about 2 tsp of nutmeg which I think, was a really nice addition. I had a little trouble with the topping. Nothing serious, it may have been my fault actually (I might have measured the butter wrong I later realized) . It wasn't crumbly at all so I added extra flour and brown sugar until it got to the consistency that I was happy with. I mixed about 1 cup of chopped pecans in the the butter/sugar mixture and evenly sprinkled it on top. I then used 1 small bag (about a cup) of whole pecans and made a boarder around the edge. (The whole pecans got toasted during the cooking process and were SO GOOD!) I then sprinkled just a little extra cinnamon and nutmeg on top. I was able to make this in the morning and cover it and chill it until that evening when I put it in the oven. DELICIOUS! This will be added to the Family Holiday Faves! Thank so so much for sharing the recipe!

I grew up not caring for sweet potatoes. My Mom was a great cook & always made sweet potato casserole with marshmallows and sometimes pineapple, oj, pecans, etc... but just didn[t care for. Found this recipe about 35 years ago and LOVE it! My children and grandchildren will not eat sweet potatoes anywhere but request this recipe at my house all the time. Most adults & kids here usually ask for seconds! #1 favorite side dish!
Wonderful recipe. Cook time is wrong. I make this every year. 1-1/2 hours it takes. Good luck, you won't be sorry. Only if you underbake and serve, as I did when I first started making this.

The very best sweet potato recipe for sure. Been making it for about a decade and always turns out absolutely delicious. Those giving it 1-star obviously need to either check their cooking skills or their taste buds.
Good, Make sure you use 4 cups cooked sweet potatoes

I serve this every Thanksgiving! Every year they say they aren't sure if its a dessert or a side dish! LOL! Only thing I change is I use 6 large sweet potatoes and bake them to bring out their natural sugars. The amounts of the other ingredients are still enough to make it plenty sweet!

I made this exactly by the recipe. It was a HUGE hit at Thanksgiving. This will be my new Sweet Potato recipe. I read the reviews and maybe next time may add some cinnamon and nutmeg but good just like it was. A little sweet for me might reduce the sugar but everyone one else loved it.
I love this recipe, my friends always ask for it on Thanksgiving. I tend to make it a little less sweeter. I also decrease the topping, and it's still amazing. I eat it for breakfast.
